specification.problem: Estimate an unknown phase phi, uniform on [0,2pi), encoded by N applications of a phase gate diag(1,e^{i phi}) distributed as n_k over M unentangled |+> probe qubits (sum n_k = N), using X-basis readout and a classical Bayesian posterior-mean estimator, scored by a circular (Holevo) error.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny non-adaptive instance: M=3 probe qubits with a sample multiplicity vector such as n=(1,2,2) (N=5) or n=(1,1,2,2); lossless; no feedback (theta_k=0); grid-search estimator. Out of scope: numerical optimization of the n_k distribution, the Bayesian bound derivation, the loss analysis and the comparison with entangled strategies, adaptive feedback, and the Shor-type resource-counting proof. The abstract gives no explicit formulas, so everything below is background or an assumed construction.

symbols.meaning: number of phase-gate applications on qubit k
total number of gate applications = queries
per-gate transmission in the loss model (outside scope; eta=1 here)

equations.label: Probe state after gates
equations.description: Each probe qubit starts in |+> and acquires phase n_k phi from n_k phase-gate applications.
equations.justification: Follows from the assumed diagonal phase gate acting n_k times on |+>; the abstract only says N gates act on M qubits in product state.
assumptions: Phase gate is diag(1,e^{i phi}) or an equivalent controlled-U with an eigenstate

equations.label: Constraint on resources
equations.description: Total number of gate placements equals the query count N.
equations.abstract_quote: where $N$ phase gates, acting on $M$ qubits prepared in a product state, may be distributed in an arbitrary way
equations.justification: The abstract says N gates are distributed arbitrarily among M qubits; the sum constraint is the natural reading.
assumptions: Each application counts as one query

equations.label: Outcome likelihood
equations.description: Outcome probabilities after H and computational-basis measurement of each qubit. With loss, cos is multiplied by eta^{n_k}.
equations.justification: Standard result for measuring (|0>+e^{i a}|1>)/sqrt2 in the X basis, where outcome 0 has probability (1+cos a)/2.

equations.label: Bayesian estimator
equations.description: Posterior mean direction with a uniform prior, computed on a G-point grid. This is a grid approximation, not exact.
equations.justification: A standard circular Bayesian estimator for a uniform prior; the paper's exact estimator is unknown.

equations.label: Error figure of merit
equations.description: Holevo-style periodic mean square error used to compare strategies. Heisenberg scaling means Delta ~ 1/N^2.
equations.abstract_quote: the optimal generalizations offer the Heisenberg $1/N^{2}$ error scaling
equations.justification: The abstract names the 1/N^2 scaling of the mean square error; the periodic error form is assumed.
assumptions: Circular variance is the error measure

registers.name: probe
registers.role: Each qubit starts in |+>, receives n_k phase-gate placements, then H and measurement; qubit k is classical bit k.

registers.name: eigenstate
registers.role: Eigenstate ancilla, only if the black box is a controlled-U. Not needed for a direct phase gate.

specification.initial_state: |+>^{\otimes M} (H on each probe qubit from |0>), no entanglement.

steps.description: Apply H to each probe qubit.
Place the black-box phase gate n_k times on qubit k (controlled on probe k with the eigenstate ancilla if a controlled-U), with total N queries.
Apply H to each probe qubit and measure all M in the Z basis, with qubit k mapped to classical bit k (Qiskit little-endian: bits[::-1][k] is b_k).
Compute the posterior over the grid and return the phase estimate.

specification.measurement: Measure all M probe qubits after H; the counts key's last character is bit 0, so b_k = key[::-1][k].
specification.classical_postprocessing: For each observed b, evaluate P(b|phi_j) on the grid, form sum_j exp(i phi_j) P(b|phi_j), take the argument mod 2pi as the estimate, and average the circular error over outcomes.
assumptions: The tiny instance M=3, n=(1,2,2) is a choice made here, not taken from the abstract
Powers of the gate are built by repeated placement, each counted as a query
Standard Kitaev n_k=2^k is the baseline
missing_information: The optimal n_k distributions and the paper's exact estimator and error measure
Exact loss model and the entangled-strategy bounds
Bayesian bound formula and the alternative resource quantification for Shor-type counting
